body: I wanted to add the Validator label but I can't seem to do that. Must only be team members that are allowed to label things?
@simensen yeah, this is a limitation of the github issue tracker currently.
@simensen Which version of PHP you are using ? There was an bug in version < 5.3.3

I'm using PHP 5.3.2.

If this is another case (symfony#898) of needing to patch for continuing to support PHP 5.3.2, I'd be happy to contribute something.

@simensen: you have packages for newer versions of php on dotdeb.org, but you'll need to recompile for Ubuntu. Otherwise you can get newer packages from newer versions of Ubuntu and also just recompile. It's not that hard.

I figure there are two ways to address this (that do not involve upgrading to PHP 5.3.3 or better). Either skip the test if it looks like it is going to fail (hopefully safe since this is a "known issue") or update the actual EmailValidator to account for this issue (pretty invasive).

I opted to take a crack at the first option. (see PR #930) I could change this so that it actually looks at PHP version as opposed to doing something that looks a little more like feature detection. Let me know if that would be more appropriate and I'll make it so.

@mvrhov This is the only issue (currently) that seems to be holding back support for PHP 5.3.2 as far as testing is concerned. Upgrading to PHP 5.3.3 seems pretty heavy handed. I know it is doable, but I have many Ubuntu 10.04 LTS hosts and trying to manage/compile PHP by hand or upgrading to another non-LTS version of Ubuntu would actually make life pretty difficult.

It is in my best interest to do what I can to help keep PHP 5.3.2 a viable option for Symfony for as long as possible. I'm hoping as long as I'm willing to do some work Symfony will find it in its best interest as well. :)
@simensen I would prefer not changing tests (as they SHOULD fail on PHP 5.3.2 as regexp used there is invalid). My proposal for fixing that issue: https://gist.github.com/970504 (not tested ;)
@stloyd Definitely the more invasive approach. :) If that is the preference I'd be happy to go that route instead.

@simensen If you are only changing the unit tests, it does not solve the issue for the validator.

@stoyld your code is broken as you overwrite the `$valid` variable totally.
@stof don't know what you mean. btw. please write my nickname correct... **stloyd** not stoyld ;)

Sorry for the typo.

the issue in your gist is line 23 as you overwrite the value. So if the host is valid the email will validate whatever the previous test returned. And you don't handle the case where there is no `@` in the URL which will throw an error in substr
I just  updated that gist, now it should handle case you mentioned properly.
Why would we be doing FILTER_VALIDATE_URL on the host?
Would something like this work? https://gist.github.com/970545 Based off of @stloyd's proposal but closer to the original.
It's kinda "protection" for `strpos` check... It's not required, as this gist is an proposal fix for discussion and it was not tested.

@simensen I just updated my gist, which is now simpler and with additional comments (yours too). I would prefer mine as it is more DRY.
@stof what you think about it ?
